summary: Tenant requests assisted safe demotion and KV-prefetch rollback after elevated tail latency and accuracy drift
description:
Issue summary: Customer LumenHealth observed increased 95p+ tail latency and transient accuracy drift on long-session clinical summarization workloads after enabling a tenant-optimizer profile (aggressive async batching + kv-prefetch + mixed-precision quant). Impact: end-user summaries had missing context in 2-4% of requests and SLA breaches for 95th percentile latency across several routes. Environment: Dedicated pool (tenant LUM-01) in us-east serving redwood-open-13b pinned to optimizer profile 'aggressive-async-v2'. Business impact: Clinical summarization is part of ingestion pipeline for downstream clinician workflows; risk of delayed notes and context loss for patient charts.

Observed behavior: Starting 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC we saw step increase in 95p latency from ~420ms to 1.6s and periodic entropy/accuracy spikes correlated with long token sequences (>3k tokens). Error rates remained low (mostly 200 responses), but token-level perplexity metrics increased and customer reported truncated or context-misaligned outputs. Expected behavior: Latency within SLA and no observable accuracy drift after optimizer changes.

Customer request: Guided, minimal-risk rollback/demote path to restore baseline economics and correctness while preserving throughput. Customer asked for explicit checklist and support to run the rollback during their maintenance window (2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Tenant LUM-01 submits long-session summarize flows (>2000 tokens) against route /v1/chat with model redwood-open-13b.
2) Optimizer profile 'aggressive-async-v2' is active (async_batch: true, batching_window: 50ms, kv_prefetch: enabled, quant_profile: q4_0_mixed).
3) Observe 95p latency and quality metrics over 5-minute sliding windows; compare to baseline snapshot taken 2026-03-11.
4) Reproduce by toggling kv-prefetch on a canary subset (~5% traffic) to see tail behaviour escalate within 10-20 minutes.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:30 UTC - Support: Confirmed correlated uptick in token-level perplexity and 95p latency coincident with tenant optimizer profile activation.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC - SRE Jordan Lee: Heap & GPU metrics normal; no OOMs; noted increased KV cache evictions per-shard when long sessions hit sequence boundaries.

2026-03-12 15:10 UTC - ENG Lucas Moreau: Hypothesis - aggressive kv-prefetch + async batching increases memory churn and cache eviction thrash for long sessions leading to recompute and quality variance with mixed quant profile.

2026-03-13 08:45 UTC - Ran controlled canary: toggling off async_batch reduced p95 by ~40% within 12 minutes; toggling off kv-prefetch restored perplexity close to baseline but increased median latency slightly.
Next steps: prepare stepwise off-ramp that minimizes request disruption: create snapshot, demote to compat profile, optionally evict tenant KV cache after warmup, monitor key metrics.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Jordan Lee (SRE): Asked for snapshot of tenant config and recent optimizer audit log. Requested permission for canary testing with 1% traffic.
2026-03-12 12:15 - LumenHealth (Customer): Approved 1% canary. Noted maintenance window preferred 2026-03-14 02:00-04:00 UTC.
2026-03-13 09:00 - Lucas Moreau (ENG): Submitted short playbook and recommended demote to 'compatibility-v1' then sequentially disable kv-prefetch, then async_batching, with KV eviction as last step.
2026-03-13 12:05 - Ethan Zhao (Assignee): Scheduling assisted rollout with customer for 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. Preparing snapshot and rollback script; tagging INT-4112 for infra coordination.
resolution: Workaround applied (planned): 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC assisted demote. Steps executed: 1) Created tenant snapshot pre-demote (snapshot id: LUM-01-snap-20260314). 2) Demoted optimizer profile from 'aggressive-async-v2' to 'compatibility-v1' for 100% of tenant traffic. 3) Disabled kv-prefetch flag and left quant_profile unchanged for canary 10% for 20 minutes. 4) After stable metrics, issued tenant KV eviction and warmed cache with controlled replay for 5 minutes. Outcome: 95p latency dropped to 540ms and perplexity returned within 3% of baseline. No increase in 5xx observed. Follow-ups: implement safety-gate that prevents aggressive combination of kv-prefetch + mixed quant for long-session tenants; schedule postmortem and add automated preflight checks.
follow_up_actions: Create preflight validator: deny optimizer profile rollouts if average session length > 1500 tokens without engineer override.
Add telemetry alert for token-eviction-rate per-tenant exceeding threshold to auto-suggest demote.
Document 'compatibility-v1' demote checklist in Confluence and link to runbook.
Schedule review with model onboarding team to test mixed-quant behavior on long sequences for redwood-open-13b.
